newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to sell T-bills for domestic debt payment.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to sell T-bills for domestic debt payment.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry said on Tuesday it will meet domestic debt maturity payments due on Wednesday by placing special treasury issues with the central bank and four other financial institutions.

"Some 24.3 billion levs are due on Wednesday for principal and interest payments on three maturing T-bill issues, and the bulk of that amount will be swapped for new issues," a ministry official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
The ministry has reached preliminary agreements with the Bulgarian Post Bank, the State Savings Bank and the State Insurance Institute for placing the new issues with them, said the official.

"The United Bulgarian Bank has already agreed to receive around 1.5 billion levs worth of new paper in exchange for payments due to it, and we expect the managers of the other three insitutions to sign the letters of acceptance," the official added.
The ministry is to receive on Wednesday some 6.5 billion levs raised at three T-bill auctions on Friday and Monday.
Those three issues with a total par value of 20 billion levs were only partly sold.
Under the Bulgarian National Bank Act, the finance ministry is entitled to a three-month credit from the BNB, which should not exceed five percent of the annual state budget revenue.
This year's credit amounts to around 6.5 billion levs, the official said.
Despite the credit from the BNB and the revenue from agreed placements, the ministry still faced a shortage of around 4.0 billion levs due on Wednesday, the official said.

The Finance Ministry was negotiating with the BNB to place with it a discount T-bill issue and another floater coupon one with a total par of some 4.0 billion levs to bridge the gap, the official said.
The official said the ministry has covered maturity payments on three-year floater coupon T-notes with a par of 500 million levs on Monday and on 18-month T-notes worth 823 million on Tuesday.

A record high main interest rate of 108 percent has stretched the budget deficit as maturity payments now exceed net sales of government securities, analysts said. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
